A cover on a wet unit traps moisture → rust, mold, and pad rot by spring. Shut down when nights stay below ~50°F and you will not need cooling again until spring. The cover is the last step, not a substitute for draining.

A cover that blocks required airflow or traps heat can damage pads and motors. Opening design balances protection with function: screened vents for off-season breathing, zippered panels for service access, and reinforced hems around cutouts so fabric does not tear at stress points.
A fitted cover that sheds water outward reduces pooling on the cabinet top; it does not replace proper flashing maintenance.
A reflective top lowers cabinet surface temperature versus bare metal or dark fabric, reducing heat soak between cycles.
A solid cover seals outdoor intakes only. If rooms stay cold, check the interior duct damper or panel inside the house — cover fabric cannot fix an open duct path.

Canvas covers use a heavier woven base (often cotton-poly blend or polyester canvas) with a rugged hand-feel. They resist abrasion and punctures better than light polyester, which matters on industrial sites and rooftop units with sharp flashing or gravel.
